anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

pass_a_gloss: And he also writes those chewing the pascha to have such a posture through the next sayings: And thus you shall eat it: your loins girded, and your shoes on your feet, and your staffs in your hands. And you shall eat it with haste. It is a pascha to the Lord.
pass_b_english: And he also writes that those [who chew] the Passover are to have [such] a posture, through the [next] words: And thus you shall [eat] it: your loins [girded], and your shoes on your feet, and your staffs in your hands. And you shall eat it in haste. It is a Passover to [the Lord].
source_text: Συγγράφει δὲ καὶ [τοιό]νδε σχῆμα ἔχειν τοὺς [τρώγο]ντας τὸ πάσχα διὰ τῶν [ἑξῆς] ῥητῶν· οὕτως δὲ φά[γεσθε] αὐτό· αἱ ὀσφύες ὑμῶν [περιε]ζωσμέναι, καὶ τὰ ὑποδή[ματα] ὑμῶν ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν ὑμῶν, || καὶ αἱ βακτηρίαι ὑμων ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν ὑμῶν. Καὶ ἔδεσθε αὐτὸ μετὰ σπουδῆς. Πάσχα ἐστὶν [Κ(υρί)ῳ.
